section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Splitting of the Sea occurred in the merit of Moshe, whose prophecy at the level of "zeh" (essential revelation) differs from other prophets' "koh" (limited illumination), allowing him to remain intact, and this same level was granted to all Israel at the Sea.
section.t: And based on this, it will also be understood why the Splitting of the Sea was in the merit of Moshe,
as it is said,
"He who splits the sea before Moshe—this is my G-d," etc.
For,
the superiority of Moshe over the other prophets is that all the prophets prophesied through "koh" (thus), while Moshe prophesied through "zeh" (this).
And there is another distinction between the prophecy of Moshe and the prophecy of the other prophets:
that when all [other] prophets prophesy, their limbs tremble and the body's strength weakens, etc.,
so that they cannot stand on their feet,
for they would fall on their faces to receive prophecy, as it is written,
"And I fell on my face," etc.
And this means that the revelation of prophecy is specifically in a manner of the stripping away of physicality,
to the extent that there was even a removal of garments at the time of prophecy,
as it is written,
"And he also stripped off his garments and prophesied... and fell naked."
Not so Moshe Rabbeinu;
even at the time of the revelation of prophecy, he stood in his place, whole.
And the explanation of this is:
that the level of prophecy of the other prophets,
the aspect of "koh"
(with the "kaf" of comparison),
is only an illumination from the concealed worlds to the revealed worlds,
not so the level of prophecy of Moshe,
the aspect of "zeh,"
is a revelation of the Essence (Atzmus).
And behold,
the revelation of the supernal light of the concealed worlds that comes through prophecy
causes the nullification of existence, like created beings returning [to their source],
and this is the matter of the stripping away of physicality at the time of prophecy.
And only Moshe Rabbeinu,
since his level of prophecy is in the aspect of the revelation of the Essence (Atzmus),
behold, by the power of the Essence (Atzmus), he was not nullified from his existence; rather, he stood in his place, whole.
And this is also the superiority of the revelation of the Splitting of the Sea,
for then there was a revelation of G-dliness for all Israel in the manner of the prophecy of Moshe.
For,
our Sages said,
"A maidservant saw at the sea what Yechezkel ben Buzi did not see in his prophecy."
And superficially, it needs to be understood:
after all, there were many miracles, signs, and wonders,

and in what way is the Splitting of the Sea specifically so elevated and sublime as to compare it to the prophecy of Yechezkel and to say that its greatness surpasses the greatness of Yechezkel's prophecy?
But the explanation is:
that the general matter of miracles is the revelation of a light that transcends the world,
from the aspect of the concealed worlds,
which therefore causes a change in the nature of the world,
in the manner and likeness of the stripping away of physicality at the time of prophecy due to the revelation of the light of the concealed worlds.
Not so the Splitting of the Sea,
which turned the sea into dry land—
that is,
not only a revelation of light from the aspect of the concealed worlds,
but moreover,
that the concealment itself came into revelation,
and this matter is specifically through the revelation of the Essence (Atzmus).
For by the power of the Essence (Atzmus), this revelation can be drawn down to souls in bodies as they stand in their place
(without the need for the stripping away of physicality),
that is,
that for all of Israel,
even a maidservant,
there was a revelation of G-dliness in the manner of the revelation of prophecy to Moshe Rabbeinu, who stood in his place, whole,
so that they pointed with a finger
and said, "This is my G-d,"
specifically "this,"
like Moshe, who prophesied through "zeh."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation at the Splitting of the Sea, though momentary, serves as preparation for future revelations in the Final Redemption and empowers the interim period, as indicated by the future tense "we will rejoice," and that the ultimate perfection will be in the Resurrection of the Dead with souls in bodies, without nullification of existence.
section.t: And behold, even though the revelation of the Splitting of the Sea was only for the moment,
it is also a preparation for the revelations that will be in the future Redemption,
and also a giving of power for the intervening time,
which is why it is said regarding "the river they will cross on foot, there we will rejoice in Him"
(which refers to the Splitting of the Sea)
in the future tense,
to indicate its continuity
(as above, section 1).
And the explanation of this is:
that "in the river they will cross on foot, there we will rejoice in Him"
also alludes to the three pilgrimage Festivals of joy, during which they would cross the river
(the Euphrates River)
and ascend for the pilgrimage to see the revelation of "the face of the L-rd,"
"to see... the face of the L-rd,"
and from this is drawn even now
(at a time when the Holy Temple does not stand)
the revelation of joy on the three Festivals,
and its extension throughout the entire year in the joy of a mitzvah.
And the mitzvot are the vessels through which and by means of which the drawing down and revelation from "sea"
(concealed worlds)
to "dry land"
(revealed worlds)
is accomplished, in a manner that the creations on dry land are not nullified from their existence
(as above, section 6),
similar to and in the likeness of the revelation of the Splitting of the Sea.
And the perfection of all these matters will be in the future Redemption,
when the matter of "the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah" will be drawn down
in revelation below,
and through this there will be a revelation of G-dliness in this physical world,
as it is said,
"And the glory of the L-rd will be revealed, and all flesh together will see," etc.,
and nevertheless, the creations will not be nullified from their existence due to the intensity of the revelation.
For,
the opinion of the Rambam
is that the primary reward of the World to Come is in a manner that has no eating or drinking, etc.,
souls without bodies,
but the teachings of Chassidus
rule in accordance with the opinion of the Ramban,
that the primary reward of the World to Come is the World of Resurrection,
specifically souls in bodies,
and nevertheless,
they will not be nullified from their existence due to the intensity of the revelation,
as at the Splitting of the Sea, where "they will cross the river on foot."
And moreover,
regarding the future, it is written, "and He will guide them in sandals,"
for,
a sandal is a garment that covers the foot,
and its meaning above is
that there are angels called "the sandal of the Shechinah,"
through whom the Divine light comes in concealment and hiding so that it can be received below.
And since in the future, our Sages said,
"In the future, the righteous
(and 'Your people are all righteous')
will be called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He,"
they too will need sandals to conceal the intensity of their level so that all the other creations below them can receive from them.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the two interpretations of the verse, showing that the revelation at the Splitting of the Sea, where they crossed on foot, is the source and guarantee for the future Redemption, when G-d will again perform wonders and guide them in sandals, leading to joy in His very Essence.
section.t: And this is also the connection and relationship between the two interpretations of the verse "He turned the sea into dry land; they will cross the river on foot," etc.:
The first interpretation, that only "He turned the sea into dry land" refers to the Splitting of the Sea,
and "in the river they will cross on foot, there we will rejoice in Him"
is in the future tense,
referring to the future to come,
and the second interpretation, that also "in the river they will cross on foot," etc., refers to the Splitting of the Sea,
because,
just as
and through the fact that all this was at the Splitting of the Sea
(according to the second interpretation),
"as in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders" in the future Redemption,
which will be
(as the haftarah of the day states):

"And the L-rd will utterly destroy the tongue of the Sea of Egypt, and He will wave His hand over the river... and He will guide them in sandals, and there will be a highway... as it was for Israel on the day of their ascent from the land of Egypt,"
and there we will rejoice in Him,
in His very Being and Essence (Atzmus),
with the coming of Mashiach Tzidkeinu, speedily in our days, Amen.
